newsitem.title: USA: Alaska settles complaint against Liggett.
newsitem.headline: Alaska settles complaint against Liggett.

text.p: Alaska has joined 22 other states in settling its legal claims against the nation's fifth-largest tobacco company, state Attorney General Bruce Botelho said Tuesday.
Alaska settled its complaints against Liggett & Myers, joining the other states that have reached agreement with the cigarette maker.

Alaska filed suit against Liggett and the other major tobacco companies on April 14, seeking reimbursement Medicaid costs used to treat smoking-related diseases and awards for alleged consumer fraud and antitrust violations.
The Alaska agreement with Liggett is identical to that reached on March 20 by the attorneys general of the 22 other states suing the tobacco industry, Botelho said.
The settlement provides no money immediately, but includes a vow by the company to disclose information about industry practices, he said.
"This agreement is an important step towards properly informing consumers of the truth about cigarettes and the consequences of smoking," Botelho said in a news release.
"The cooperation of Liggett provided for in this settlement will also be valuable in Alaska's prosecution of claims against other tobacco companies," he said.
Meanwhile, state lawmakers here were considering a bill that would make Alaska's tobacco tax the highest in the nation.

The state Senate has already passed the bill, which would hike taxes on cigarettes by 71 cents a pack and impose a similar tax increase on other tobacco products. The state already has a 29-cent-per-pack tax.
The House was scheduled to vote on the bill Thursday.
